desc: Derive walk structure (bounces cost 2 and grant a visit to the neighbor; end at n−1 or n−2) and the carry-greedy feasibility argument
Implement the complete `Solution.maxScore`: carry-greedy `check(T)` + binary-search driver in the starter-code format

Validate on the provided examples ([2,4], m=3 → 4; [1,2,3], m=5 → 2) plus edge cases: m < n (cost ≥ n for any T>0 ⇒ answer 0), n=2 with m=1 (→ 0), hi = (m//n+1)·max(points) provably infeasible and > 0 even when m < n

Confirm optimality of the greedy (exchange argument: deferring a bounce to the next index costs the same 2 moves but additionally grants a free visit to i+2; last index cheaper to reach by a forward step, 2k−1, than by k bounces from n−2, 2k) — matches the canonical solution shape for this problem
Check performance: O(n) per check × ~50 binary-search iterations ≈ 2.5M simple ops with early `cost > m` abort; acceptable
